text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our assessment of your hypertension, could you please tell me your age and describe any symptoms you have been experiencing, such as headaches, vision changes, or decreased exercise tolerance?

text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. Since he is asymptomatic and this was found incidentally, I need to check his vital signs; specifically, what were the blood pressure readings taken today, and do you have his height and weight to calculate his BMI percentile?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
High blood pressure in a 5-year-old, especially if isolated to one arm, strongly suggests a structural vascular issue. I need to assess for signs of coarctation of the aorta, so please check his pulses in all four extremities and measure blood pressure in both arms and both legs.

REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Echocardiogram: Findings: Narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation. Left ventricular function is normal. Abdominal Ultrasound: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
